    "## Data Understanding\n",
    "The yellow taxi trip records include fields capturing pick-up and drop-off dates/times, pick-up and drop-off locations, trip distances, itemized fares, rate types, payment types, and driver-reported passenger counts.\n",
    "\n",
    "The data is stored in Parquet format (*.parquet*). The dataset is from 2009 to 2024. However, for this assignment, we will only be using the data from 2023.\n",
    "\n",
    "The data for each month is present in a different parquet file. You will get twelve files for each of the months in 2023.\n",
    "\n",
    "The data was collected and provided to the NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) by technology providers like vendors and taxi hailing apps. <br>\n",
    "\n",
    "You can find the link to the TLC trip records page here: https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "LI6qC5IDxZU1"
   },
   "source": [
    "###  Data Description\n",
    "You can find the data description here: [Data Dictionary](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/tlc/downloads/pdf/data_dictionary_trip_records_yellow.pdf)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "FafCzrDuxHg2"
   },
   "source": [
    "**Trip Records**\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "|Field Name       |description |\n",
    "|:----------------|:-----------|\n",
    "| VendorID | A code indicating the TPEP provider that provided the record. <br> 1= Creative Mobile Technologies, LLC; <br> 2= VeriFone Inc. |\n",
    "| tpep_pickup_datetime | The date and time when the meter was engaged.  |\n",
    "| tpep_dropoff_datetime | The date and time when the meter was disengaged.   |\n",
    "| Passenger_count | The number of passengers in the vehicle. <br> This is a driver-entered value. |\n",
    "| Trip_distance | The elapsed trip distance in miles reported by the taximeter. |\n",
    "| PULocationID | TLC Taxi Zone in which the taximeter was engaged |\n",
    "| DOLocationID | TLC Taxi Zone in which the taximeter was disengaged |\n",
    "|RateCodeID |The final rate code in effect at the end of the trip.<br> 1 = Standard rate <br> 2 = JFK <br> 3 = Newark <br>4 = Nassau or Westchester <br>5 = Negotiated fare <br>6 = Group ride |\n",
    "|Store_and_fwd_flag |This flag indicates whether the trip record was held in vehicle memory before sending to the vendor, aka “store and forward,” because the vehicle did not have a connection to the server.  <br>Y= store and forward trip <br>N= not a store and forward trip |\n",
    "|Payment_type| A numeric code signifying how the passenger paid for the trip. <br> 1 = Credit card <br>2 = Cash <br>3 = No charge <br>4 = Dispute <br>5 = Unknown <br>6 = Voided trip |\n",
    "|Fare_amount| The time-and-distance fare calculated by the meter. <br>Extra Miscellaneous extras and surcharges.  Currently, this only includes the 0.50 and 1 USD rush hour and overnight charges. |\n",
    "|MTA_tax |0.50 USD MTA tax that is automatically triggered based on the metered rate in use. |\n",
    "|Improvement_surcharge | 0.30 USD improvement surcharge assessed trips at the flag drop. The improvement surcharge began being levied in 2015. |\n",
    "|Tip_amount |Tip amount – This field is automatically populated for credit card tips. Cash tips are not included. |\n",
    "| Tolls_amount | Total amount of all tolls paid in trip.  |\n",
    "| total_amount | The total amount charged to passengers. Does not include cash tips. |\n",
    "|Congestion_Surcharge |Total amount collected in trip for NYS congestion surcharge. |\n",
    "| Airport_fee | 1.25 USD for pick up only at LaGuardia and John F. Kennedy Airports|\n",
    "\n",
    "Although the amounts of extra charges and taxes applied are specified in the data dictionary, you will see that some cases have different values of these charges in the actual data."
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "How many rows are there? Do you think handling such a large number of rows is computationally feasible when we have to combine the data for all twelve months into one?\n",
    "\n",
    "To handle this, we need to sample a fraction of data from each of the files. How to go about that? Think of a way to select only some portion of the data from each month's file that accurately represents the trends."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "zHx7lh_3QGmj"
   },
   "source": [
    "#### Sampling the Data\n",
    "> One way is to take a small percentage of entries for pickup in every hour of a date. So, for all the days in a month, we can iterate through the hours and select 5% values randomly from those. Use `tpep_pickup_datetime` for this. Separate date and hour from the datetime values and then for each date, select some fraction of trips for each of the 24 hours.\n",
    "\n",
    "To sample data, you can use the `sample()` method. Follow this syntax:\n",
    "\n",
    "```Python\n",
    "# sampled_data is an empty DF to keep appending sampled data of each hour\n",
    "# hour_data is the DF of entries for an hour 'X' on a date 'Y'\n",
    "\n",
    "sample = hour_data.sample(frac = 0.05, random_state = 42)\n",
    "# sample 0.05 of the hour_data\n",
    "# random_state is just a seed for sampling, you can define it yourself\n",
    "\n",
    "sampled_data = pd.concat([sampled_data, sample]) # adding data for this hour to the DF\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "This *sampled_data* will contain 5% values selected at random from each hour.\n",
    "\n",
    "Note that the code given above is only the part that will be used for sampling and not the complete code required for sampling and combining the data files.\n",
    "\n",
    "Keep in mind that you sample by date AND hour, not just hour. (Why?)"
   ]
  },

    "# Sample the data\n",
    "# It is recommmended to not load all the files at once to avoid memory overload\n",
    "SAMPLE_FRACTION = 0.05\n",
    "RANDOM_STATE = 42\n",
    "\n",
    "sampled_months = []\n",
    "\n",
    "for file_path in PARQUET_FILES:\n",
    "    print(f\"Reading {file_path.name}...\")\n",
    "\n",
    "    month_df = pd.read_parquet(file_path)\n",
    "\n",
    "    month_df[\"tpep_pickup_datetime\"] = pd.to_datetime(\n",
    "        month_df[\"tpep_pickup_datetime\"],\n",
    "        errors=\"coerce\"\n",
    "    )\n",
    "\n",
    "    month_df = month_df.dropna(subset=[\"tpep_pickup_datetime\"]).copy()\n",
    "\n",
    "    month_df[\"pickup_date\"] = month_df[\"tpep_pickup_datetime\"].dt.date\n",
    "    month_df[\"pickup_hour\"] = month_df[\"tpep_pickup_datetime\"].dt.hour\n",
    "\n",
    "    month_sample = (\n",
    "        month_df\n",
    "        .groupby([\"pickup_date\", \"pickup_hour\"], group_keys=False)\n",
    "        .apply(\n",
    "            lambda group: group.sample(\n",
    "                frac=SAMPLE_FRACTION,\n",
    "                random_state=RANDOM_STATE\n",
    "            )\n",
    "        )\n",
    "        .reset_index(drop=True)\n",
    "    )\n",
    "\n",
    "    sampled_months.append(month_sample)\n",
    "\n",
    "    print(\n",
    "        f\"  Original rows: {len(month_df):,} | \"\n",
    "        f\"Sampled rows: {len(month_sample):,}\"\n",
    "    )\n",
    "\n",
    "df = pd.concat(sampled_months, ignore_index=True)\n",
    "\n",
    "df.drop(columns=[\"pickup_date\"], inplace=True, errors=\"ignore\")\n",
    "df.reset_index(drop=True, inplace=True)\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Combined sampled rows: {len(df):,}\")\n",
    "print(f\"Combined columns: {df.shape[1]}\")\n"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "# Take a small percentage of entries from each hour of every date.\n",
    "# Iterating through the monthly data:\n",
    "#   read a month file -> day -> hour: append sampled data -> move to next hour -> move to next day after 24 hours -> move to next month file\n",
    "# Create a single dataframe for the year combining all the monthly data\n",
    "\n",
    "# Select the folder having data files\n",
    "import os\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "\n",
    "DATA_FOLDER = Path.cwd()\n",
    "\n",
    "# Approximately 275,000 rows from around 38 million records\n",
    "SAMPLE_FRACTION = 0.0072 # 5% will produce 1.9 million records, so reducing it to 0.72% \n",
    "\n",
    "# Fixed seed makes the sample reproducible\n",
    "RANDOM_STATE = 42\n",
    "\n",
    "# Create a list of all the twelve files to read\n",
    "file_list = sorted([\n",
    "    file_name\n",
    "    for file_name in os.listdir(DATA_FOLDER)\n",
    "    if file_name.lower().endswith('.parquet')\n",
    "])\n",
    "\n",
    "# initialise an empty dataframe\n",
    "#df = pd.DataFrame()\n",
    "# Initialise an empty list.\n",
    "# A list is more efficient than repeatedly concatenating DataFrames.\n",
    "yearly_samples = []\n",
    "\n",
    "# iterate through the list of files and sample one by one:\n",
    "for file_name in file_list:\n",
    "    try:\n",
    "        # file path for the current file\n",
    "        file_path = os.path.join(DATA_FOLDER, file_name)\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Reading the current file\n",
    "        print(f\"\\nReading: {file_name}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Read the monthly Parquet file\n",
    "        monthly_data = pd.read_parquet(file_path)\n",
    "\n",
    "        print(f\"Original rows: {len(monthly_data):,}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "        # We will store the sampled data for the current date in this df by appending the sampled data from each hour to this\n",
    "        # After completing iteration through each date, we will append this data to the final dataframe.\n",
    "        #sampled_data = pd.DataFrame()\n",
    "\n",
    "        # --------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "        # Convert pickup datetime into date and hour\n",
    "        # --------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "\n",
    "        monthly_data['tpep_pickup_datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(\n",
    "            monthly_data['tpep_pickup_datetime'],\n",
    "            errors='coerce'\n",
    "        )\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Remove rows where the pickup datetime could not be converted\n",
    "        monthly_data = monthly_data.dropna(\n",
    "            subset=['tpep_pickup_datetime']\n",
    "        ).copy()\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Create date and hour fields\n",
    "        monthly_data['pickup_date'] = (\n",
    "            monthly_data['tpep_pickup_datetime'].dt.date\n",
    "        )\n",
    "\n",
    "        monthly_data['pickup_hour'] = (\n",
    "            monthly_data['tpep_pickup_datetime'].dt.hour\n",
    "        )\n",
    "\n",
    "        # --------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "        # Sample records from every date-hour group\n",
    "        # --------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "\n",
    "        sampled_data = []\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Iterate through each date\n",
    "        for selected_date, date_data in monthly_data.groupby(\n",
    "            'pickup_date',\n",
    "            sort=True\n",
    "        ):\n",
    "\n",
    "            # Iterate through every hour present on that date\n",
    "            for selected_hour, hourly_data in date_data.groupby(\n",
    "                'pickup_hour',\n",
    "                sort=True\n",
    "            ):\n",
    "\n",
    "                # Sample a small percentage from the current hour\n",
    "                # If a group contains very few records, this may\n",
    "                # produce zero rows, which is acceptable.\n",
    "                sampled_hour = hourly_data.sample(\n",
    "                    frac=SAMPLE_FRACTION,\n",
    "                    random_state=RANDOM_STATE\n",
    "                )\n",
    "\n",
    "                # Store the sampled records from this hour\n",
    "                sampled_data.append(sampled_hour)\n",
    "\n",
    "        # Combine all sampled hourly data from this month\n",
    "        if sampled_data:\n",
    "            monthly_sample = pd.concat(\n",
    "                sampled_data,\n",
    "                ignore_index=True\n",
    "            )\n",
    "\n",
    "            # Add the monthly sample to the yearly list\n",
    "            yearly_samples.append(monthly_sample)\n",
    "\n",
    "            print(f\"Sampled rows: {len(monthly_sample):,}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "    except Exception as e:\n",
    "        print(f\"Error reading file {file_name}: {e}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# ------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "# Combine all twelve monthly samples into one yearly DataFrame\n",
    "# ------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "\n",
    "if yearly_samples:\n",
    "    df = pd.concat(\n",
    "        yearly_samples,\n",
    "        ignore_index=True\n",
    "    )\n",
    "else:\n",
    "    df = pd.DataFrame()\n",
    "\n",
    "# Remove helper columns if they are not required for analysis\n",
    "df = df.drop(\n",
    "    columns=['pickup_date', 'pickup_hour'],\n",
    "    errors='ignore'\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Shuffle the final yearly sample\n",
    "df = df.sample(\n",
    "    frac=1,\n",
    "    random_state=RANDOM_STATE\n",
    ").reset_index(drop=True)\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"\\nSampling completed.\")\n",
    "print(f\"Final yearly sample rows: {len(df):,}\")\n",
    "print(f\"Final number of columns: {len(df.columns)}\")"
   ]
  },
  {

    "#Lets ensure date time columns are converted to date time\n",
    "datetime_columns = [\n",
    "    \"tpep_pickup_datetime\",\n",
    "    \"tpep_dropoff_datetime\"\n",
    "]\n",
    "\n",
    "for column in datetime_columns:\n",
    "    sampled_df[column] = pd.to_datetime(sampled_df[column], errors=\"coerce\")\n",
    "\n",
    "sampled_df[\"trip_duration_minutes\"] = (\n",
    "    sampled_df[\"tpep_dropoff_datetime\"] -\n",
    "    sampled_df[\"tpep_pickup_datetime\"]\n",
    ").dt.total_seconds() / 60\n",
    "\n",
    "sampled_df[\"pickup_hour\"] = sampled_df[\"tpep_pickup_datetime\"].dt.hour\n",
    "sampled_df[\"pickup_day\"] = sampled_df[\"tpep_pickup_datetime\"].dt.day_name()\n",
    "sampled_df[\"pickup_day_number\"] = sampled_df[\"tpep_pickup_datetime\"].dt.dayofweek\n",
    "sampled_df[\"pickup_month\"] = sampled_df[\"tpep_pickup_datetime\"].dt.month\n",
    "sampled_df[\"pickup_month_name\"] = sampled_df[\"tpep_pickup_datetime\"].dt.month_name()\n",
    "sampled_df[\"pickup_quarter\"] = sampled_df[\"tpep_pickup_datetime\"].dt.quarter\n",
    "\n",
    "sampled_df[\"day_type\"] = np.where(\n",
    "    sampled_df[\"pickup_day_number\"] >= 5,\n",
    "    \"Weekend\",\n",
    "    \"Weekday\"\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "sampled_df[\"time_of_day\"] = pd.cut(\n",
    "    sampled_df[\"pickup_hour\"],\n",
    "    bins=[-1, 5, 11, 16, 20, 23],\n",
    "    labels=[\n",
    "        \"Night\",\n",
    "        \"Morning\",\n",
    "        \"Afternoon\",\n",
    "        \"Evening\",\n",
    "        \"Late evening\"\n",
    "    ]\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "sampled_df[\"trip_speed_mph\"] = np.where(\n",
    "    sampled_df[\"trip_duration_minutes\"] > 0,\n",
    "    sampled_df[\"trip_distance\"] / (sampled_df[\"trip_duration_minutes\"] / 60),\n",
    "    np.nan\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "sampled_df[\"fare_per_mile\"] = np.where(\n",

    "    sampled_df[\"fare_amount\"] / sampled_df[\"trip_distance\"],\n",

    "    sampled_df[\"fare_amount\"] > 0,\n",
    "    100 * sampled_df[\"tip_amount\"] / sampled_df[\"fare_amount\"],\n",
    "    np.nan\n",
    ")\n",

   "source": [
    "# Passenger count:\n",
    "# Use the median of positive values rather than filling with zero.\n",
    "passenger_median = sampled_df.loc[\n",
    "    sampled_df[\"passenger_count\"].between(1, 6),\n",
    "    \"passenger_count\"\n",
    "].median()\n",
    "\n",
    "sampled_df[\"passenger_count\"] = sampled_df[\"passenger_count\"].fillna(passenger_median)\n",
    "sampled_df.loc[sampled_df[\"passenger_count\"] <= 0, \"passenger_count\"] = passenger_median\n",
    "\n",
    "# Rate code:\n",
    "# Missing rate codes are treated as the standard rate.\n",
    "sampled_df[\"rate_code_id\"] = sampled_df[\"rate_code_id\"].fillna(1)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Monetary fields:\n",
    "# Missing surcharge or tax values generally indicate that the charge was not applied.\n",
    "monetary_columns = [\n",
    "    \"extra\",\n",
    "    \"mta_tax\",\n",
    "    \"tip_amount\",\n",
    "    \"tolls_amount\",\n",
    "    \"improvement_surcharge\",\n",
    "    \"congestion_surcharge\",\n",
    "    \"airport_fee_combined\"\n",
    "]\n",
    "\n",
    "for column in monetary_columns:\n",
    "    if column in sampled_df.columns:\n",
    "        sampled_df[column] = sampled_df[column].fillna(0)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Remove records missing essential fields.\n",
    "essential_columns = [\n",
    "    \"tpep_pickup_datetime\",\n",
    "    \"tpep_dropoff_datetime\",\n",
    "    \"trip_distance\",\n",
    "    \"fare_amount\",\n",
    "    \"total_amount\",\n",
    "    \"pu_location_id\",\n",
    "    \"do_location_id\"\n",
    "]\n",
    "\n",
    "sampled_df.dropna(subset=essential_columns, inplace=True)\n"
   ]

    "Notes on Rate Code ID:\n",
    "The negative-fare records were examined by comparing their RatecodeID values. Some records contained unusual or unknown rate codes, but RatecodeID itself is categorical and should not be corrected by replacing it with zero. Since negative fares and charges are invalid for completed-trip revenue analysis, records containing negative monetary values were excluded. Unknown rate codes were retained and treated separately to avoid unnecessarily removing potentially informative trips."

    "| `trip_distance`         | Numerical (Continuous)                                            | Measured in miles, can take any decimal value                                                                                                  |\n",

    "| `pickup_hour`           | Categorical (Ordinal) — sometimes treated as Numerical (Discrete) | Represents hour of day (0–23); has a natural order but is often used as a grouping variable rather than a quantity to sum/average meaningfully |\n",

    "Compiled Findings — General Analysis Summary\n",
    "\n",
    "Temporal Trends\n",
    "Busiest hours: Bimodal distribution with peaks around the morning commute (approx. 8–9 AM) and evening commute/nightlife hours (approx. 6–9 PM), with the lowest activity between 3–5 AM.\n",
    "Busiest days: Weekday activity is generally strong, with Friday and Saturday showing elevated volumes, consistent with combined commuter and social/nightlife travel.\n",
    "Busiest months: Trip volume is fairly consistent across months, with minor dips likely tied to seasonal factors (e.g., winter weather, holiday periods).\n",
    "\n",
    "Revenue Trends\n",
    "Monthly revenue: Total revenue tracks closely with trip volume trends, showing relative stability across months with no extreme outlier months.\n",
    "Quarterly revenue: Revenue is fairly evenly distributed across quarters, suggesting no strong seasonal revenue concentration, though later quarters may show marginal growth if ridership trends upward toward year-end.\n",
    "\n",
    "Fare Relationships\n",
    "Fare vs. trip distance: Strong positive correlation — fare increases predictably with distance, as expected from metered pricing, with some scatter due to flat-rate airport trips and surcharges.\n",
    "Fare vs. trip duration: Also positively correlated, though weaker than distance, since time-based charges apply mainly during slow traffic/idling.\n",
    "Fare vs. passenger count: Very weak or negligible correlation — fare is driven by distance/time, not number of riders, since NYC taxi fares aren't per-passenger.\n",
    "\n",
    "Tipping Behavior\n",
    "Tip vs. trip distance: Positive correlation — longer trips tend to generate higher tip amounts in absolute terms, though tip percentage may vary independently and is influenced heavily by payment type (credit card tips are recorded; cash tips are not).\n",
    "\n",
    "Geographic Patterns\n",
    "Busiest zones: Trip volume is heavily concentrated in Manhattan (particularly Midtown, Upper East Side, and Union Square/Gramercy areas) and the two major airports (JFK and LaGuardia), while outer-borough zones (parts of Staten Island, eastern Queens, and the Bronx) show substantially lower pickup activity.\n",
    "Payment behavior geography: Credit card usage is disproportionately higher in Manhattan and airport zones, likely reflecting business travelers and tourists."

   "source": [
    "# Find routes which have the slowest speeds at different times of the day\n",
    "\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "\n",
    "# Ensure trip_duration is in hours (adjust based on your unit — assuming minutes here)\n",
    "financial_df['trip_duration_hr'] = financial_df['trip_duration'] / 60\n",
    "\n",
    "# Group by route (pickup zone -> dropoff zone) and hour, get avg distance & avg duration\n",
    "route_speed = (\n",
    "    financial_df.groupby(['pu_location_id', 'do_location_id', 'pickup_hour'])\n",
    "    .agg(\n",
    "        avg_distance=('trip_distance', 'mean'),\n",
    "        avg_duration_hr=('trip_duration_hr', 'mean'),\n",
    "        trip_count=('trip_distance', 'count')\n",
    "    )\n",
    "    .reset_index()\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Keep only statistically reliable routes (avoid noise from 1-2 trip routes)\n",
    "route_speed = route_speed[route_speed['trip_count'] >= 5]\n",
    "\n",
    "# Speed formula: distance / average duration for that hour\n",
    "route_speed['speed_mph'] = route_speed['avg_distance'] / route_speed['avg_duration_hr']\n",
    "\n",
    "# Attach zone names for readability\n",
    "route_speed = route_speed.merge(\n",
    "    taxi_zones[['LocationID', 'zone']], left_on='pu_location_id', right_on='LocationID'\n",
    ").rename(columns={'zone': 'pickup_zone'}).drop(columns='LocationID')\n",
    "\n",
    "route_speed = route_speed.merge(\n",
    "    taxi_zones[['LocationID', 'zone']], left_on='do_location_id', right_on='LocationID'\n",
    ").rename(columns={'zone': 'dropoff_zone'}).drop(columns='LocationID')\n",
    "\n",
    "# Top 15 slowest routes overall\n",
    "slowest_routes_overall = route_speed.sort_values('speed_mph').head(15)\n",
    "print(\"Overall slowest routes:\")\n",
    "display(slowest_routes_overall[['pickup_zone', 'dropoff_zone', 'pickup_hour', 'speed_mph', 'trip_count']])\n",
    "\n",
    "# Slowest route for EACH hour of day\n",
    "slowest_per_hour = (\n",
    "    route_speed.sort_values('speed_mph')\n",
    "    .groupby('pickup_hour')\n",
    "    .first()\n",
    "    .reset_index()\n",
    ")\n",
    "print(\"\\nSlowest route at each hour:\")\n",
    "display(slowest_per_hour[['pickup_hour', 'pickup_zone', 'dropoff_zone', 'speed_mph', 'trip_count']])\n",
    "\n",
    "# Visualize the trend of minimum speed across the day\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "\n",
    "hourly_min_speed = route_speed.groupby('pickup_hour')['speed_mph'].min()\n",
    "hourly_min_speed.plot(kind='line', marker='o', figsize=(10, 5), color='crimson')\n",

    "How does identifying high-traffic, high-demand routes help us?"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Operational efficiency: Enables proactive driver repositioning ahead of predictable congestion windows, minimizing idle time and improving fleet utilization.\n",
    "\n",
    "Pricing strategy: Justifies time-based surcharges or dynamic pricing on routes/hours where drivers spend disproportionate time relative to distance, keeping driver earnings fair without overcharging customers unnecessarily.\n",
    "\n",
    "Customer experience: Produces more accurate ETA and fare estimates, reducing dissatisfaction from underestimated trip times on known bottleneck routes.\n",
    "\n",
    "Infrastructure/policy insight: Flags recurring congestion corridors to city planners as candidates for signal optimization, dedicated lanes, or congestion pricing.\n",
    "\n",
    "Driver guidance: Helps in-app routing suggest alternatives that avoid known slow segments at specific hours, improving driver earnings per hour.\n",
    "\n",
    "Demand-supply matching: Highlights corridors with high demand so vehicles can be positioned in advance, reducing missed pickups and passenger wait times."

    "# Scale up the number of trips\n",
    "\n",
    "# Fill in the value of your sampling fraction and use that to scale up the numbers\n",
    "sample_fraction = 0.0072  # 0.72% sample\n",
    "\n",
    "# Count number of trips per hour from the sample\n",
    "trips_per_hour = financial_df['pickup_hour'].value_counts().sort_index()\n",
    "\n",
    "# Scale up counts to estimate actual citywide trip volume\n",
    "scaled_trips_per_hour = (trips_per_hour / sample_fraction).round(0).astype(int)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Find the five busiest hours (by scaled count), sorted descending\n",
    "top_5_busiest_hours = scaled_trips_per_hour.sort_values(ascending=False).head(5)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Display results\n",
    "print(\"Actual (scaled) number of trips in the five busiest hours:\\n\")\n",
    "for hour, count in top_5_busiest_hours.items():\n",
    "    print(f\"Hour {hour:02d}:00  →  {count:,} trips\")\n",
    "\n"
   ]

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Explanation:\n",
    "\n",
    "trips_per_hour holds the raw sample counts for each hour of the day.\n",
    "Dividing by sample_fraction (0.0072) scales each hourly count up to an estimate of the true citywide trip volume, since the sample represents only 0.72% of the actual data.\n",
    "Sorting the scaled counts in descending order and taking the top 5 gives the five busiest hours along with their estimated actual trip counts."

    "# Find the top 10 and bottom 10 pickup/dropoff ratios\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 1: Merge pickup and dropoff counts on zone ID ---\n",
    "ratio_df = pickup_counts[['pu_location_id', 'pickup_count', 'zone', 'borough']].merge(\n",
    "    dropoff_counts[['do_location_id', 'dropoff_count']],\n",
    "    left_on='pu_location_id', right_on='do_location_id', how='outer'\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Fill missing counts with 0 (zones that only appear as pickup or only as dropoff)\n",
    "ratio_df['pickup_count'] = ratio_df['pickup_count'].fillna(0)\n",
    "ratio_df['dropoff_count'] = ratio_df['dropoff_count'].fillna(0)\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 2: Filter out zones with very low volume to avoid unstable ratios ---\n",
    "MIN_TRIPS = 20\n",
    "ratio_df = ratio_df[(ratio_df['pickup_count'] + ratio_df['dropoff_count']) >= MIN_TRIPS]\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 3: Compute ratio (avoid division by zero) ---\n",
    "ratio_df['pickup_dropoff_ratio'] = ratio_df['pickup_count'] / ratio_df['dropoff_count'].replace(0, 0.5)\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 4: Top 10 highest and lowest ratios ---\n",
    "top10_highest_ratio = ratio_df.sort_values('pickup_dropoff_ratio', ascending=False).head(10)\n",
    "top10_lowest_ratio = ratio_df.sort_values('pickup_dropoff_ratio', ascending=True).head(10)\n",

    "# Filter for night hours (11 PM to 5 AM)\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 1: Define night hours (11 PM to 5 AM) ---\n",
    "night_hours = [23, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 2: Create a time-of-day category ---\n",
    "financial_df['time_period'] = financial_df['pickup_hour'].apply(\n",
    "    lambda h: 'Night' if h in night_hours else 'Day'\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 3: Calculate total revenue per period ---\n",
    "# Using total_amount as the revenue metric (captures fare + tips + surcharges/tolls)\n",
    "revenue_by_period = financial_df.groupby('time_period')['total_amount'].sum().reset_index()\n",
    "revenue_by_period.columns = ['time_period', 'total_revenue']\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 4: Calculate revenue share (%) ---\n",
    "total_revenue = revenue_by_period['total_revenue'].sum()\n",
    "revenue_by_period['revenue_share_pct'] = (\n",
    "    revenue_by_period['total_revenue'] / total_revenue * 100\n",
    ").round(2)\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 5: Also compute trip counts and average fare per period for context ---\n",
    "trip_counts = financial_df.groupby('time_period').size().reset_index(name='trip_count')\n",
    "avg_fare = financial_df.groupby('time_period')['total_amount'].mean().reset_index(name='avg_fare_per_trip')\n",
    "\n",
    "summary = revenue_by_period.merge(trip_counts, on='time_period').merge(avg_fare, on='time_period')\n",
    "summary['trip_share_pct'] = (summary['trip_count'] / summary['trip_count'].sum() * 100).round(2)\n",
    "\n",
    "print(summary[['time_period', 'trip_count', 'trip_share_pct',\n",
    "                'total_revenue', 'revenue_share_pct', 'avg_fare_per_trip']])\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 6: Visualize revenue share ---\n",
    "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))\n",
    "\n",
    "axes[0].pie(\n",
    "    summary['total_revenue'],\n",
    "    labels=summary['time_period'],\n",
    "    autopct='%1.1f%%',\n",
    "    colors=['#f4a261', '#264653'],\n",
    "    startangle=90\n",
    ")\n",
    "axes[0].set_title(\"Revenue Share: Day vs Night\")\n",

    "# Analyse the fare per mile per passenger for different passenger counts\n",
    "\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 1: Filter out invalid records ---\n",
    "# Remove trips with zero/negative distance, zero/negative fare, or zero passengers\n",
    "valid_trips = financial_df[\n",
    "    (financial_df['trip_distance'] > 0) &\n",
    "    (financial_df['fare_amount'] > 0) &\n",
    "    (financial_df['passenger_count'] > 0)\n",
    "].copy()\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 2: Calculate fare per mile for each trip ---\n",
    "valid_trips['fare_per_mile'] = valid_trips['fare_amount'] / valid_trips['trip_distance']\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 3: Group by passenger count, get average fare per mile ---\n",
    "fare_per_mile_by_pax = (\n",
    "    valid_trips.groupby('passenger_count')['fare_per_mile']\n",
    "    .mean()\n",
    "    .reset_index(name='avg_fare_per_mile')\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 4: Divide by passenger count to get fare per mile per passenger ---\n",
    "fare_per_mile_by_pax['fare_per_mile_per_passenger'] = (\n",
    "    fare_per_mile_by_pax['avg_fare_per_mile'] / fare_per_mile_by_pax['passenger_count']\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Step 5: Add trip counts for context (statistical reliability check) ---\n",
    "trip_counts_by_pax = valid_trips.groupby('passenger_count').size().reset_index(name='trip_count')\n",
    "fare_per_mile_by_pax = fare_per_mile_by_pax.merge(trip_counts_by_pax, on='passenger_count')\n",
    "\n",
    "# Optional: filter out passenger counts with very few trips (unreliable, e.g. 7,8,9 pax)\n",
    "MIN_TRIPS = 20\n",
    "fare_per_mile_by_pax_reliable = fare_per_mile_by_pax[fare_per_mile_by_pax['trip_count'] >= MIN_TRIPS]\n",
    "\n",
    "print(fare_per_mile_by_pax_reliable[\n",
    "    ['passenger_count', 'trip_count', 'avg_fare_per_mile', 'fare_per_mile_per_passenger']\n",
    "].round(3))\n",

    "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))\n",

    "import numpy as np\n",
    "\n",
    "# =========================================================\n",
    "# Prep: base fare-per-mile column (reusable for 3.2.10 & 3.2.11)\n",
    "# =========================================================\n",
    "valid_trips = financial_df[\n",
    "    (financial_df['trip_distance'] > 0) &\n",
    "    (financial_df['fare_amount'] > 0)\n",

    "# --- Combined heatmap: hour x day of week ---\n",

    "# Defining distance tiers\n",
    "\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "import seaborn as sns\n",
    "\n",
    "# ---- Defining distance tiers ----\n",
    "tier_df = sampled_df_clean[sampled_df_clean[\"trip_distance\"] > 0].copy()\n",
    "\n",
    "def distance_tier(d):\n",
    "    if d <= 2:\n",
    "        return \"Short (<=2 mi)\"\n",
    "    elif d <= 5:\n",
    "        return \"Medium (2-5 mi)\"\n",
    "    else:\n",
    "        return \"Long (>5 mi)\"\n",
    "\n",
    "tier_df[\"distance_tier\"] = tier_df[\"trip_distance\"].apply(distance_tier)\n",
    "\n",
    "tier_order = [\"Short (<=2 mi)\", \"Medium (2-5 mi)\", \"Long (>5 mi)\"]\n",
    "tier_df[\"distance_tier\"] = pd.Categorical(\n",
    "    tier_df[\"distance_tier\"], categories=tier_order, ordered=True\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Ensure fare_per_mile exists\n",
    "tier_df[\"fare_per_mile\"] = tier_df[\"fare_amount\"] / tier_df[\"trip_distance\"]\n",
    "\n",
    "# ---- Average fare per mile by vendor and tier ----\n",
    "fare_tier_vendor = (\n",
    "    tier_df.groupby([\"distance_tier\", \"vendor_id\"])[\"fare_per_mile\"]\n",
    "    .agg([\"mean\", \"median\", \"count\"])\n",
    "    .reset_index()\n",
    "    .rename(columns={\n",
    "        \"mean\": \"avg_fare_per_mile\",\n",
    "        \"median\": \"median_fare_per_mile\",\n",
    "        \"count\": \"trip_count\"\n",
    "    })\n",
    ")\n",
    "print(fare_tier_vendor.round(3))\n",
    "\n",
    "pivot_tier_vendor = fare_tier_vendor.pivot(\n",
    "    index=\"distance_tier\", columns=\"vendor_id\", values=\"avg_fare_per_mile\"\n",
    ")\n",
    "print(\"\\nPivoted view (avg fare per mile):\\n\", pivot_tier_vendor.round(3))\n",
    "\n",
    "# ---- Visualization ----\n",
    "pivot_tier_vendor.plot(kind=\"bar\", figsize=(10, 6), colormap=\"viridis\")\n",
    "plt.title(\"Average Fare per Mile by Distance Tier and Vendor\")\n",
    "plt.xlabel(\"Distance Tier\")\n",
    "plt.ylabel(\"Fare per Mile (USD/mile)\")\n",
    "plt.xticks(rotation=0)\n",
    "plt.legend(title=\"Vendor ID\")\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "plt.show()\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))\n",
    "sns.boxplot(\n",
    "    data=tier_df, x=\"distance_tier\", y=\"fare_per_mile\",\n",
    "    hue=\"vendor_id\", showfliers=False\n",
    ")\n",
    "plt.title(\"Fare per Mile Distribution by Distance Tier and Vendor\")\n",
    "plt.xlabel(\"Distance Tier\")\n",
    "plt.ylabel(\"Fare per Mile (USD/mile)\")\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "plt.show()\n"
   ]

    "#  Analyze tip percentages based on distances, passenger counts and pickup times\n",
    "\n",
    "tip_df = sampled_df_clean[\n",
    "    (sampled_df_clean[\"fare_amount\"] > 0) &\n",
    "    (sampled_df_clean[\"trip_distance\"] > 0)\n",
    "].copy()\n",
    "\n",
    "tip_df[\"tip_pct\"] = (tip_df[\"tip_amount\"] / tip_df[\"fare_amount\"]) * 100\n",
    "tip_df = tip_df[(tip_df[\"tip_pct\"] >= 0) & (tip_df[\"tip_pct\"] <= 100)]\n",
    "\n",
    "tip_df[\"distance_tier\"] = tip_df[\"trip_distance\"].apply(distance_tier)\n",
    "tip_df[\"distance_tier\"] = pd.Categorical(\n",
    "    tip_df[\"distance_tier\"], categories=tier_order, ordered=True\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- By distance tier ---\n",
    "tip_by_distance = tip_df.groupby(\"distance_tier\")[\"tip_pct\"].mean().reset_index(name=\"avg_tip_pct\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- By passenger count (filter for reliability, min 20 trips) ---\n",
    "tip_by_passenger = tip_df.groupby(\"passenger_count\")[\"tip_pct\"].mean().reset_index(name=\"avg_tip_pct\")\n",
    "trip_counts_pax = tip_df.groupby(\"passenger_count\").size().reset_index(name=\"trip_count\")\n",
    "tip_by_passenger = tip_by_passenger.merge(trip_counts_pax, on=\"passenger_count\")\n",
    "tip_by_passenger_reliable = tip_by_passenger[tip_by_passenger[\"trip_count\"] >= 20]\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- By pickup hour ---\n",
    "tip_by_hour = tip_df.groupby(\"pickup_hour\")[\"tip_pct\"].mean().reset_index(name=\"avg_tip_pct\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# --- Visualization ---\n",
    "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 5))\n",
    "\n",
    "axes[0].bar(tip_by_distance[\"distance_tier\"].astype(str), tip_by_distance[\"avg_tip_pct\"], color=\"seagreen\")\n",
    "axes[0].set_title(\"Avg Tip % by Distance Tier\")\n",
    "axes[0].set_xlabel(\"Distance Tier\")\n",
    "axes[0].set_ylabel(\"Average Tip %\")\n",
    "\n",
    "axes[1].bar(tip_by_passenger_reliable[\"passenger_count\"].astype(str), tip_by_passenger_reliable[\"avg_tip_pct\"], color=\"steelblue\")\n",
    "axes[1].set_title(\"Avg Tip % by Passenger Count\")\n",
    "axes[1].set_xlabel(\"Passenger Count\")\n",
    "axes[1].set_ylabel(\"Average Tip %\")\n",
    "\n",
    "axes[2].plot(tip_by_hour[\"pickup_hour\"], tip_by_hour[\"avg_tip_pct\"], marker=\"o\", color=\"darkorange\")\n",
    "axes[2].set_title(\"Avg Tip % by Pickup Hour\")\n",
    "axes[2].set_xlabel(\"Hour of Day\")\n",

   "source": [
    "Factors Leading to low top percentages:\n",
    "\n",
    "| Factor                        | Effect on tip %                           | Likely explanation                                                                                                                  |\n",
    "| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n",
    "| Longer trip distance          | Tip % decreases as distance increases     | Tip generosity doesn't scale linearly with fare; riders round to flat amounts on long trips                                         |\n",
    "| Higher passenger count        | Tip % decreases as group size increases   | Cost-splitting psychology reduces individual tipping incentive                                                                      |\n",
    "| Late-night hours (~2 AM–5 AM) | Noticeable dip in average tip %           | Higher share of cash payments during these hours; cash tips are not recorded in the dataset, mechanically dragging the average down |\n",
    "| Payment type (cash)           | Near-zero average tip % for cash payments | Confirms the late-night dip is a **data reporting bias**, not genuine rider behavior                                                |"
   ]

    "# Compare trips with tip percentage < 10% to trips with tip percentage > 25%\n",
    "\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "import seaborn as sns\n",
    "\n",
    "# Base dataframe: valid fare & distance, tip_pct already computed as in 3.2.13\n",
    "compare_df = tip_df.copy()\n",
    "\n",
    "low_tip = compare_df[compare_df[\"tip_pct\"] < 10]\n",
    "high_tip = compare_df[compare_df[\"tip_pct\"] > 25]\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Low-tip trips (<10%): {len(low_tip):,}\")\n",
    "print(f\"High-tip trips (>25%): {len(high_tip):,}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# ---- Numeric feature comparison ----\n",
    "numeric_cols = [\n",
    "    \"trip_distance\", \"fare_amount\", \"tip_amount\",\n",
    "    \"passenger_count\", \"fare_per_mile\"\n",
    "]\n",
    "\n",
    "comparison = pd.DataFrame({\n",
    "    \"low_tip_mean\": low_tip[numeric_cols].mean(),\n",
    "    \"high_tip_mean\": high_tip[numeric_cols].mean(),\n",
    "})\n",
    "comparison[\"difference\"] = comparison[\"high_tip_mean\"] - comparison[\"low_tip_mean\"]\n",
    "comparison[\"pct_diff\"] = (comparison[\"difference\"] / comparison[\"low_tip_mean\"]) * 100\n",

    "print(\"\\nNumeric feature comparison:\\n\", comparison.round(3))\n",

    "    print(\"\\nPayment type distribution (%):\\n\", payment_dist)\n",

    "| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n",
    "| Fare per mile decreases as trip distance increases (fixed-charge dilution) | Consider a modest minimum-distance surcharge or fare floor adjustment for very short trips to better cover fixed dispatch costs, without altering the competitive metered structure for longer trips                                                                                                                                     |\n",
    "| Fare per mile per passenger drops as occupancy increases                   | Introduce a shared-ride/pooled pricing tier or small per-passenger surcharge, capturing more revenue per vehicle-mile on higher-occupancy trips without pricing out any single rider                                                                                                                                                     |\n",
    "| Night trips are low-volume but carry higher average fares/revenue-per-trip | Maintain or slightly reinforce existing night/overnight surcharge levels — they're already an efficient way to monetize a low-volume window without needing broader fare hikes                                                                                                                                                           |\n",
    "| Surcharges concentrate in rush hour and Manhattan-core zones               | This is already effectively a de facto dynamic pricing mechanism; formalize it further by tying surge/extra-charge intensity more tightly to real-time congestion data rather than fixed time windows, to stay competitive while still capturing peak-demand value                                                                       |\n",
    "| Fares are largely vendor-agnostic and metered                              | Since base pricing is regulated and not a meaningful differentiator, competitive edge should come from **service-level factors** (wait time, ETA accuracy, vehicle availability) rather than undercutting fares — reinforcing that the routing/positioning recommendations above directly support the pricing strategy's competitiveness |\n",
    "| Tip percentage data is biased by cash payment underreporting at night      | Exclude or caveat tip-based profitability metrics for night hours when making revenue decisions, since apparent \"low-tip\" periods are partly a reporting artifact, not a true demand signal                                                                                                                                              |"
